report:
The corrected manuscript establishes original P16.5 in the explicitly retained full-big domain: every actual big rational line bundle on every smooth integral projective variety of dimension n≥1 over every algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field. The additional zero-volume result covers the entire numerically trivial rational-bundle range, including nontorsion Pic⁰. This verdict concerns the complete theorem, both appendices, and its replacement foundations; it does not import an accepted nonample S–M package.

I treated G0 solely as the supplied actual-ample theory and G1 solely as relative generation and its single FS-net consequence. I read the supplied bodies and checked those scopes at each application. Historical verdicts, bindings, source registers and compilation claims supplied no mathematical evidence.

1. Sections 2–3 establish the original all-point cone. The ample embedding uses actual ample bundle differences and weight-zero generating systems, preserving the scalar at every supported point. The added ample floors produce one decreasing defining net. The section-minorant argument fixes its positive class margin before selecting an incoming tail. It first proves order on U and then extends order by ample divisorial determination. The old-pole lemma uses a comparison extension with value −∞, rather than subtracting two infinite values. Its quantitative bound supplies the compact tail selection used twice in the flattening construction. The special stages are directed, their classes approach θ, and their infimum equals the requested endpoint at every point. Genuine envelopes therefore precede compactness. The separator theorem identifies divisorial tail suprema; the generic coordinate is retained separately. No countable cofinal extraction is used.

2. Section 4 reconstructs full-section energy. Proper normal section descent and the homogeneous finite flag give the literal lattice and all time monomials in (4.1)–(4.2). All-large-cleared-degree section asymptotics justify the intercept limit, rather than only a limsup. Volume differentiation gives the finite coefficient measures with their factors b_E, independence of the large time twist, and raw mass V. Exceptional refinement coefficients vanish by normal extension across codimension two. The continuous-obstacle filtration has closed endpoints and finitely many jumps; rank-scaled trace bounds justify its C⁰ extension. The section-envelope equivalence proves E(P(f))=𝓔(f), including E(R)=0. The outer infimum defines energy on the entire genuine cone. The finite supporting planes in (4.7) give weak upper semicontinuity and concavity; compact majorant selection gives decreasing continuity. These conclusions do not assume an equation or a mixed operator.

3. Section 5 and Appendix A identify the actual complete moving systems. The cofinality argument works in every positive power: on a common determination, each nef competitor is moved into the ample interior while its complementary class becomes big; complete-system injections then dominate that competitor. Real competitors follow by interior rational approximation. Directed bounded positive-product compactness and fixed signed tests justify (5.1). This argument does not presume multilinearity of big positive products.

The corrected (5.2) is the full absolute moving bundle on the required common refinements. Only the horizontal common fixed factor is divided out. The residual bundle retains T_m^ver, and removal of its effective residual central base divisor gives a generated nef bundle. The infinity endpoints and all intervening time monomials recover the entire generic section space. Normality verifies both section-extension implications, not merely numerical equality. Further refinements preserve this full section-space construction. Consequently (5.3)–(5.4), the restricted construction (9.2), and subsequent maxima and rational tensors use the same actual generic A_m and fixed factor. Compact-uniform density on U follows from the increasing full-system stages and decreasing finite G1 stages with the same endpoint. In (5.5), the term min(f)(V−V_m) is correctly retained through the degree limit and removed only after the moving limit at fixed finite f, before the outer infimum.

Appendix A’s surface calculation is correct. For L=H+E on Bl_p P², the complete section space is s_E^m H⁰(mH). After blowing up E×{0} and taking D=−B, every full original weight is zero. Horizontal division leaves H+cF, hence auxiliary energy zero and measure δ_v₀. The different bundle H−B+cF is generated for c≥1. Its central restrictions have squares zero and one. With B=P(N∨), N=O_E(−1)⊕O_E, the stated convention gives B³=1; its cube is 3c−1. Thus its energy is −1/3 and its measure is δ_ord_E. The example establishes precisely why deleting the vertical term changes the actual system.

4. Section 6’s finite estimates are valid with raw masses. The SNC row identities give (6.1), positivity and Cauchy–Schwarz. Principalization of the two signed ideals gives the absolute-value divisor and quadratic contraction. Direct telescoping verifies the tangent multiplicity n−j in (6.2). The midpoint kernel gives both constants in (6.3); the slot-change recursion gives the exponents in (6.4). The absolute estimate (6.5) retains its generic term until the moving limit. The nonnegative mixed terms give (6.6), and the physical minorant together with the retained trace error proves genuine contraction (6.7). The pole series is decreasing, has finite generic value and bounded energy cost, and has the asserted pole wherever the original test has a pole and R is finite. It supplies an actual E¹ pole for Z.

5. Section 7 proves the original outer derivative with both signs. The deficient trace is convex in c, and c>B/V establishes genuine bigness. Ordered full-filtration weights give coefficientwise domination, with missing mass at most B/c. The fixed nef upper tests control the volume loss on refinements and establish the two signed psef margins. The additional path restriction (7.2) is necessary and sufficient for the shifted nonpositive obstacles; the rough cost bound alone would not suffice. Passing the complete increment at fixed c and t, then taking signed derivatives and finally c→∞, proves uniqueness of the canonical cluster. Uniform model approximation gives every C⁰ direction. Ordered secant bounds give decreasing weak continuity. The envelope-output identification follows from equal envelope energies and both derivative signs. The effective-divisor moment estimate proves algebraic nullness and the original collar bound without using output integrability.

6. Section 8’s pre-attainment steps are noncircular. The intrinsic target condition uses relative costs R−u on the locus where R is finite and separately excludes reference-pole mass. The converse integrability argument uses genuine decreasing convex sums and ordinary countable monotone convergence. Contraction then supplies coercivity. For canonical model envelopes, the increasing relative costs are continuous on U. Directed Radon integration follows from finite covers of compact subsets of strict superlevels; it is not measurable-net monotone convergence. Model near-maximizer outputs tend weakly to the target by both approximate stationarity signs, before attainment. The finite absolute estimate first passes bounded changing quotient tests on fixed U cutoffs. It then proves output integrability, and only afterward extends to arbitrary genuine tests by uniform ordered canonical errors. The target version uses the already constructed pre-attainment weak output approximation. Exact contact integrals and this fixed-test passage establish the whole supporting planes (8.4).

7. Section 9’s full/subspace/quotient traces are exact. The quotient Lipschitz constant is V−V_A; differentiation and the constant law make the missing-volume functional positive, giving the stated total variation exactly. The restricted lattice retains T^ver and is the full auxiliary lattice, verified by horizontal and central orders. Its zero-volume case is handled by rank growth, without differentiating a nonbig class. For positive volume, complete-base-system Fujita applies to the fixed actual restricted bundle. A fixed globally nef big upper class satisfying both signed test conditions supplies the uniform Morse constant. Passing top volumes first and using both signs proves the derivative squeeze (9.5). The ordered-energy estimate, fixed-test quadratic bound, and separate auxiliary and original collars establish (9.6)–(9.9). Genuine floors provide bounded physical identification; no original E¹ membership is assigned to a physical stage.

8. Sections 10–11 construct the entire genuine mixed operator. The finite unisolvent matrices are fixed before any limit. Their inverses pass finite nef coefficients to positive symmetric original measures with mass V and raw component multiplicities. Bounded relative order handles all real simplex weights. Independent genuine decreasing approximation and fixed secant brackets establish choice independence and decreasing weak continuity. Mixed domination and the uniform canonical-test errors prove genuine weighted continuity, including independently changing genuine tests. Fixed-cutoff finite telescoping then gives the full raw identity (10.2).

The energy-complete filter imposes only individual energy and generic errors together with cofinality conditions. Its directedness follows by selecting a common sufficiently large cleared multiple for each finite tuple. At a fixed cap, the ordered cap estimates compare a changing lower stage to a fixed canonical upper index. The degree limit precedes the upper-index limit; total-variation truncation is removed last. Barycenter energy completion is derived from the finite plane and absolute estimate, rather than inserted into admissibility. Fixed coefficient inversion therefore gives every mixed coefficient. Equation (11.3) is correctly a paired changing physical quotient moment.

The stronger fixed-original-unbounded-test assertion remains unproved. Neither term of (11.4) has been shown to vanish in absolute physical-output integral, and this audit does not claim otherwise. It is unnecessary for the literal original completion criteria: bounded full-system identification constructs the operator, Section 10 proves its genuine weighted continuity, and Section 11 proves the needed physical weak approximation independence. Sections 8 and 12 pass unbounded tests through genuine canonical error estimates and fixed-target Radon integration. None of these steps requires fixed-original-unbounded convergence at every physical auxiliary output. No supported infinite difference is used.

9. Section 12 proves attainment and every-solution uniqueness. The finite four-point estimate follows from top-power telescoping, graph Cauchy–Schwarz and slot change; equal raw masses cancel constants. Bounded physical midpoint identification and genuine weighted continuity pass it to all actual E¹ endpoints. Near-maximizer midpoint gaps give uniform Cauchy estimates on every weak energy sublevel. The limit at each fixed unbounded test is identified before taking the supremum, using fixed bounded canonical tests, uniform output errors, and directed Radon integration at the intrinsic target. Finite divisorial coordinate continuity then gives target-integral net continuity on compact energy sublevels. Coercivity, weak compactness and energy upper semicontinuity yield an actual original maximizer. Both C⁰ stationarity signs yield the equation. Whole planes make every solution a maximizer; midpoint vanishing and independently intrinsic divisorial Dirac targets separate any two normalized solutions. Ample all-point determination extends equality through supported poles.

10. Sections 13–14 prove the claimed locality and nullness. The bounded maximum uses the same actual fixed factor and generated quotient systems. Constant shifts preserve the scalar winner and raw operator. For independent genuine nets, the fixed ramp in (13.2) has the stated wrong-winner implication and error bound. Weak limits are taken at fixed ramp parameters; uniform absolute canonical errors then allow the upper-index limit, followed by an ordinary ramp sequence. This proves strict Borel locality without declaring unbounded winning sets open. Displaced maxima and equal raw masses give comparison. Negligible-set transfer is literal on the same all-point ample carrier; the ample pole is tensored back into an actual big bundle and converted to an E¹ pole. Its pole locus gives a Borel null superset, so the non-Borel outer-null assertion is established.

11. The numerical-zero theorem is valid for nontorsion Pic⁰ as well. It uses the actual ample bundles L+εA, not sections of L. Integer tensoring and one fixed ample coordinate bound force every normalized zero-class potential to vanish at every divisorial coordinate; all-point determination makes it constant everywhere. The entire classified cone has zero energy, zero raw operator and the literal zero target, with uniqueness modulo constants. The P¹×P¹ example correctly obstructs uniqueness for the nonzero zero-volume class with the raw top equation. That larger range is explicitly excluded, as the supplied criteria permit. Appendix B supplies provenance only; none of its historical claims is needed for the theorem.

Primary evidence was independently opened. The following are browser-rendered line coordinates, not inherited author-ledger coordinates: premises 0–2, [BFJ v2](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0608260v2), L250–268, L310–441 and L445–545; premise 3, [BJ v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4), L3996–4022, PDF page 57; premise 4, the same version, L10614–10647, PDF page 132. The complete finite Hodge/slot unit L2705–3107 was also read and checked against the reconstructed calculation. Premises 5–6, [Lazarsfeld–Mustaţă v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0805.4559v1), L567–617, L780–810, L1005–1175, L1414–1610 and L1629–1631; the latter explicitly removes uncountability for Fujita. Premise 7, [Bierstone–Milman](https://archive.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/2624/1/preprint_2007_30.pdf), Theorems 1.1/1.3 at L42–63/L153–179, definitions L83–96, and pertinent calculus and proof units L406–1449. Premises 8 and 12, [Lazarsfeld’s published excerpt](https://beckassets.blob.core.windows.net/product/readingsample/389723/9783540225331_excerpt_001.pdf), L1869–1892, L1936–2083, L2808–2826, L2961–2998, L3115–3196, L3363–3438, L3527–3553, L3824–3826 and L5113–5440. Premises 9–11, [Stacks 01PR](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PR), L91–135; [02KH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02KH), L23–54; [03H2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03H2), L23–41. The [Addendum v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.07183v2), L128–257, independently matches the section calculation within G1; no nonample closure theorem was imported from it.

Ordinary background applications were checked with their actual hypotheses. Normal section descent and exceptional extension follow from height-one orders and normal extension across codimension two. Kodaira section subtraction follows from positive full-section growth against the lower-dimensional hyperplane restriction bound. The elementary algebraic Morse inequality follows by telescoping section restrictions to a generated ample divisor, then nef approximation; this checks the input in BFJ’s uniform remainder proof. The surface Hodge base case and the finite-semigroup conductor/counting steps underlying the retrieved units were also checked independently. Compactness and Radon arguments use compact Hausdorff spaces and fixed finite masses, with no metrizability assumption.

Harmless wording corrections: in the bounded theorem’s proof, “f_j↓ν_m” means “f_j↓u_m”; Appendix B’s reference to the corrected moving formula “(5.4)” should be “(5.2)”; Appendix A’s “exactly” prescribed fixed factor means divisibility by the common fixed factor, allowing additional zeros of individual sections; and (8.1)’s supremum is over normalized E¹ potentials, as its surrounding target definition requires. Real constant shifts are obtained by uniform rational shifts and the proved constant/continuity laws. These do not change the constructions or require a new argument.

premises: On smooth projective varieties over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields, positive products of big real Cartier classes are the least upper bounds of products of dominated nef Cartier classes on common determinations. They are continuous on the big cone, monotone and agree with nef intersections. Positive Weil classes bounded by a fixed ample intersection class form a weakly compact set. BFJ, math/0608260v2, §§1–2.

On a smooth projective d-fold over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, volume is continuous, vanishes outside the big cone and on its boundary, equals the top positive product on pseudoeffective classes, has concave d-th root, and is C¹ on the big cone with derivative d⟨α^(d−1)⟩·H. BFJ, math/0608260v2, §§2–3.

For nef Cartier β and fixed nef big Cartier ω on a smooth projective d-fold over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, if β≤ω in pseudoeffective order and ω±H are nef, then vol(β+tH)≥β^d+d t β^(d−1)·H−Kt² for |t|≤1, with K depending only on d and ω^d. BFJ, math/0608260v2, Corollary 3.4 and its signed application.

For an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field and an ample class ω, each divisorial valuation v admits a continuous PL separator ψ satisfying sup(φ−ψ)=(φ−ψ)(v) for every ω-psh φ. Consequently a bounded-above family’s raw supremum and usc regularization agree at v. BJ, 1801.08229v4, Theorem 5.6 and Lemma 5.7.

On an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, if an ample class has the envelope property, every negligible subset—contained in the discrepancy between a bounded-above psh family’s raw supremum and its usc regularization—is contained in the pole locus of a genuine ample-psh potential. No Borel assumption on the subset is required. BJ, 1801.08229v4, Theorem 13.17.

For every actual big integral bundle N on a smooth integral projective d-fold over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, d!h⁰(mN)/m^d converges to vol(N) as m→∞. For a rational bundle, the corresponding limit holds through all sufficiently large denominator-cleared degrees. Lazarsfeld–Mustaţă, 0805.4559v1, Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 2.3.

For an actual big rational bundle N on a smooth integral projective d-fold over any algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, resolve each complete nonempty |mN| and write p_m*(mN)=M_m+G_m with M_m generated and G_m effective. Then (M_m/m)^d converges to vol(N) through all sufficiently large cleared degrees, hence along divisibility-cofinal degrees, without finite generation of the section ring. Lazarsfeld–Mustaţă, 0805.4559v1, Theorem 3.3 and Remarks 3.4/3.7.

In characteristic zero, quasiprojective varieties admit functorial resolution, and coherent ideals on smooth varieties admit functorial principalization compatible with an SNC boundary, by finite projective blowups with smooth admissible centers. The constructions preserve the open locus where the specified data already require no modification and are functorial for smooth morphisms; consequently invariant data for a smooth G_m action have equivariant constructions. Bierstone–Milman, Functoriality in resolution of singularities, Theorems 1.1/1.3.

For projective varieties over algebraically closed fields, ampleness of an actual rational bundle depends only on its numerical class. The ample cone is open and is the interior of the nef cone; the nef cone is its closure. The sum of an ample real class and a nef real class is ample. Lazarsfeld, Positivity in Algebraic Geometry I, §§1.2–1.4.

If X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, A is an ample invertible sheaf, and F is a finite-type quasi-coherent sheaf, then F⊗A^m is globally generated for every sufficiently large integer m. Stacks Project, Proposition 28.27.13, condition (7).

For a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism f, a quasi-coherent sheaf F, and any flat base change g, the base-change maps g*R^i f*F→R^i f′*F′ are isomorphisms for all i≥0. In particular full section spaces commute with field extension for the projective schemes and actual bundles at issue. Stacks Project, Lemma 30.5.2.

For a proper birational morphism p:Y→Z of normal integral noetherian varieties, p*O_Y=O_Z as a pushforward, and pullback identifies H⁰(Z,N) with H⁰(Y,p*N) for every actual line bundle N. Stacks Project, Theorem 37.53.5, with normality and birationality, and projection formula.

For nef real Cartier classes α and β on a smooth projective d-fold over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, mixed intersections satisfy Khovanskii–Teissier inequalities; in particular ((α+β)^d)^(1/d)≥(α^d)^(1/d)+(β^d)^(1/d). Lazarsfeld, Positivity in Algebraic Geometry I, Theorem 1.6.1, Variant 1.6.2 and Corollary 1.6.3.
